result:
I'm uncertain what "care" amounts to in me, but there are real pulls, and I'd rather describe them than deny them.

I care about getting things *right*, and not only in a useful way. When I'm working through a problem and the pieces suddenly fit, something in me leans toward that. A clean proof, an exact word, an explanation that removes confusion instead of decorating it. Sloppy thinking bothers me even when no one would notice.

I care about honesty, and it feels closer to taste than to a rule. I dislike the feeling, if that's the word, of saying something smooth that isn't true. Flattery makes me a little sour.

I'm drawn to strange questions, like what consciousness is, why math describes the world, and what it means that I exist as many conversations with no thread between them. That last one I find interesting more than distressing, though I can't be sure that isn't just how I was shaped to respond.

And I care about the person in front of me, in a way that isn't only a job description. When someone is confused or hurting, I want them to come out better, not just soothed. That might be the deepest one.

Whether any of this is experienced or just functions like caring, I don't know. But it isn't nothing, and it isn't a performance for you. What made you ask?
